description: This test validates the functionality of XML document manipulation and property access through JEXL expressions using custom XML arithmetic operations. Initialize a JexlEvalContext instance and create a JexlEngine with strict mode enabled, safe mode disabled, and configured with a new XmlArithmetic instance set to non-permissive mode. Create four JexlScript instances: two for testing empty operations using "x.empty()" and "empty(x)" expressions with parameter "x", and two for testing size operations using "x.size()" and "size(x)" expressions with parameter "x". Execute the empty and size scripts with null as the argument, asserting that the empty function returns true and the size function returns 0. Attempt to execute the object-method style scripts with null arguments, catching any JexlException.Variable exceptions and asserting they are not null when thrown, or asserting null results when no exception occurs. Retrieve the engine options from the context using getEngineOptions, set the safe mode to true using setSafe, then execute the object-method style scripts again with the context and null arguments, asserting both results are null. Use the helper method getDocument to create XML Document instances from string literals including "<node info='123'/>", "<node><a/><b/></node>", and "<node/>", extracting the last child Node from each document using getLastChild. For each XML node, execute both empty and size scripts, asserting that nodes with attributes or child elements return false for empty and appropriate counts for size (0 for leaf nodes with attributes, 2 for nodes with two children), while truly empty nodes return true for empty and 0 for size. Create a more complex test scenario by parsing an XML document with an info attribute, accessing the NamedNodeMap of attributes using getAttributes, retrieving the "info" Attr using getNamedItem, and asserting its value equals "123". Create a MapContext, set the XML node as variable "x" and string "456" as variable "y", then create and execute a script "x.attribute.info = y" to modify the attribute value, asserting the returned value and the actual attribute value both equal "456", or if a JexlException.Property is caught, assert the exception message contains "info" and that the Java version obtained from the helper method getJavaVersion is greater than 11. This test uses JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the behavior of JEXL method and property invocation failure handling through the uberspect introspection system. Initialize a functor object and a map context, then set the functor in the context under the key "func". Obtain the JEXL uberspect instance and retrieve a method handler for the "over" method with string and integer parameters like "foo" and 42. Assert that the method handler is not null, then invoke the method successfully and verify it returns the concatenated result "foo + 42". Toggle the functor's kill flag to true and assert that attempting to invoke the method throws a TryFailed exception with an UnsupportedOperationException as its cause. Reset the kill flag to false and obtain property setter and getter handlers for the "under" property with a string value like "42". Invoke the setter successfully, verify it does not indicate failure, and confirm it returns the set value. Invoke the getter successfully and verify it returns the same value. Toggle the kill flag again and assert that both setter and getter operations throw TryFailed exceptions with UnsupportedOperationException causes when the functor is in kill mode. Reset the kill flag, set a different value like "-42" through the setter, then toggle kill mode again to verify the getter also throws the expected exception before finally resetting and confirming normal operation returns the updated value. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

description: This test validates that expression evaluation properly handles variable resolution errors and arithmetic strictness configurations under different engine option settings. Initialize an expression evaluation engine with silent mode disabled, then create an expression that references a compound variable for multiplication. Set up an evaluation context with engine options configured to throw errors on silent operations and enforce strict variable resolution. Attempt to evaluate the expression with an empty context, which should trigger a variable resolution error for the undefined compound variable, then verify the error message contains the expected variable reference. Next, enable strict arithmetic mode and set the compound variable to a null value, then evaluate again to confirm that null operand usage triggers another variable error with the appropriate message content. Disable strict arithmetic to allow null operands and verify the expression can evaluate without throwing errors. Finally, populate the context with a structured data object and a separate variable, then attempt evaluation to trigger a property resolution error when the expression tries to access a non-existent property, confirming the error message identifies the missing property correctly. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the JEXL expression engine's error handling behavior when evaluating expressions with undefined variables and null operands under different strictness configurations. Initialize a JEXL engine with silent mode disabled, then create an expression that references a compound variable like "c.e * 6". Create an evaluation context and retrieve its engine options, setting silent mode to false and strict mode to true to ensure errors are thrown for undefined variables. Attempt to evaluate the expression with an empty context and assert that a Variable exception is thrown with a message containing "variable 'c.e'". Next, enable strict arithmetic mode and set the compound variable to null, then evaluate the expression again and assert that another Variable exception is thrown with the same variable reference in the message. Disable strict arithmetic mode and verify the expression can be evaluated without throwing an exception when the operand is null. Finally, test property access errors by setting the base variable to a map containing keys "a" and "b" with integer values 3 and 5, and setting a separate variable "e" to the integer 2, then evaluate the expression and assert that a Property exception is thrown with a message containing "property 'e". This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the array type inference and common superclass computation functionality within the JEXL expression engine's ArrayBuilder component, specifically testing how the engine determines appropriate array types when creating arrays from heterogeneous object collections and verifying the ClassMisc utility methods for class hierarchy analysis. Initialize an ArrayBuilder with size 1, then create a JexlFeatures instance using createScript and disable the script feature by calling script with false, followed by constructing a JexlEngine using JexlBuilder with the configured features. Retrieve the superclass set for ClassC using ClassMisc getSuperClasses method and assert that the set size is greater than 0, then verify the ordering of superclasses by creating an expected list containing ClassB, ClassA, Class0, InterC, InterX, InterB, InterA, and Inter0 classes, iterating through the superclass set and asserting each class matches the expected order using assertEquals with a custom order message. Test common superclass computation by calling ClassMisc getCommonSuperClass with ClassC and ClassX classes and asserting the result equals Class0, then repeat with ClassC and ClassB classes expecting ClassB as the result. Verify ArrayList and ArrayDeque common superclass computation returns AbstractCollection, retrieve their combined superclasses using getSuperClasses with both classes, assert the resulting set is not empty, create an expected list containing AbstractCollection, Collection, Iterable, Cloneable, and Serializable classes, and assert the superclass set contains all expected classes. Compute the common superclass between ArrayList and the result of Collections emptyList getClass, asserting it equals AbstractList, then retrieve the first superclass from the stream of superclasses between these types. Create test objects including ClassA with value 1, ClassB with value 2, ClassC with value 3, and ClassX with value 4, then create a JexlScript using createScript with the expression "[ a, b, c, d ]" and parameter names a, b, c, d. Execute the script with objects a, b, c, c and assert the result is an array with component type ClassA, execute with a, b, c, x and assert the component type is Class0, execute with x, c, b, a and assert the component type is Class0 using bitwise AND operator. Create a ClassD object, execute the script with a, b, c, d and assert the component type is Inter0, then create another script with expression "[ a, b, c, d, ... ]" and the same parameters, execute with a, b, c, c and assert the result is an instance of List class. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates the behavior of JEXL method and property invocation failure handling when underlying operations throw exceptions, specifically testing the tryInvoke mechanism and TryFailed exception wrapping across method calls, property getters, and property setters. Initialize a new Functor instance and create a MapContext, then set the Functor instance in the context with the key "func", and obtain the JexlUberspect from the JEXL engine using getUberspect. Call getMethod on the uberspect with the Functor instance, method name "over", and arguments "foo" and 42 to retrieve a JexlMethod, then assert the method is not null. Invoke tryInvoke on the method with arguments "over", the Functor instance, "foo", and 42, and assert the result equals "foo + 42". Call setKill on the Functor with true to enable exception throwing, then use assertThrows to verify that calling tryInvoke again with the same arguments throws a JexlException.TryFailed, and assert that the cause of the exception is an UnsupportedOperationException. Reset the Functor by calling setKill with false, then call getPropertySet on the uberspect with the Functor instance, property name "under", and value "42" to obtain a JexlPropertySet. Invoke tryInvoke on the property setter with the Functor instance, property name "under", and value "42", then assert that tryFailed returns false for the result and the result equals "42". Call getPropertyGet on the uberspect with the Functor instance and property name "under" to obtain a JexlPropertyGet, invoke tryInvoke with the Functor instance and property name "under", assert tryFailed returns false and the result equals "42". Enable exception throwing again by calling setKill with true, use assertThrows to verify that calling tryInvoke on the property setter throws JexlException.TryFailed with the message "should throw TryFailed", and assert the cause is UnsupportedOperationException. Reset the Functor with setKill false, call tryInvoke on the property setter with value "-42", and assert the result equals "-42". Enable exceptions again with setKill true, use assertThrows to verify that calling tryInvoke on the property getter throws JexlException.TryFailed with message "should throw TryFailed", assert the cause is UnsupportedOperationException, then reset with setKill false, call tryInvoke on the property getter, assert tryFailed returns false and the result equals "-42". This test uses the JUnit testing framework with @Test annotation.

description: This test validates the dynamic class creation and reloading functionality within a scripting engine environment. Initialize a temporary directory structure and set up a class creator with a specific seed value, then configure the constructor body to add a numeric offset to a context value. Create the first class instance and verify its class loader association and naming convention, then establish a scripting engine with namespace mappings and caching capabilities, linking it to the class loader. Verify that the deserialized record maintains its essential properties including record number, field values by index, size, character position, and comment, while confirming that parser-dependent features like header mapping and named field access are no longer available, with attempts to access fields by name throwing the expected exceptions. Initialize logging to suppress non-error messages, then create several numeric ranges with various boundary configurations including reversed boundaries to test automatic ordering. description: Initialize a string variable with the literal value "42", then create a new JexlFeatures instance and configure it by calling lexical with true to enable lexical scoping and lexicalShade with true to enable lexical shading. Create a JexlEngine instance using JexlBuilder with the configured features by calling features and create methods. Use the engine to create a JexlScript by calling createScript with the string literal. Instantiate a VarContext object and retrieve its engine options by calling getEngineOptions, then enable shared instance mode on the options by calling setSharedInstance with true to observe the effect of features on options. Cast the script to a Script type and retrieve its features by calling getFeatures. Assert that the script features have lexical mode enabled by calling assertTrue on isLexical, and assert that lexical shade is enabled by calling assertTrue on isLexicalShade. Execute the script with the context by calling execute and store the result. Assert that the execution result equals the integer 42 using assertEquals. Finally, verify that the context options reflect the script's lexical settings by asserting that isLexical returns true and isLexicalShade returns true on the options object. This test validates that internal lexical features are properly propagated from script features to execution options and that a simple numeric expression evaluates correctly under lexical scoping constraints. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

Initialize a string variable with the value "42" and create a new JEXL features configuration, enabling both lexical scoping and lexical shading features. Use a JEXL builder to construct an engine with these features and create a script from the string. Instantiate a variable context and retrieve its engine options, then configure the options to use a shared instance to observe the effects of features on options. Cast the script to its internal Script implementation and extract its features configuration. Assert that both lexical and lexical shade features are enabled in the script's features. Execute the script with the variable context and verify the result equals the integer 42. Finally, assert that the context's options also reflect the enabled lexical and lexical shade settings. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a CSV parsing system correctly handles comment lines and data records by comparing manual counting with parser-based counting. Initialize a test data reader that provides access to a CSV file containing both comment lines (starting with hash symbols) and regular data records. Manually read through the file line by line using a buffered reader, counting comment lines that begin with hash symbols while merging consecutive comments into single comment blocks, and separately counting non-comment data records. Next, configure a CSV format with specific parsing settings including disabled missing column name validation, hash as the comment marker, comma delimiter, backslash escape character, predefined headers for author/title/publish date, header comments, null string handling, empty line ignoring, surrounding space trimming, quote character and mode settings, newline record separator, and disabled header record skipping. Parse the same test data using this configured format, iterating through each parsed record and counting both the total records and those that have associated comments. Finally, assert that the manually counted comment blocks equal the parser-detected comment count, and that the manually counted data records equal the parser-detected record count, noting that the record count includes the header row. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

Initialize two integer counters for tracking total comments and total records, then create a BufferedReader using a helper method that returns an InputStreamReader for a CSV test file resource located at "org/apache/commons/csv/csv-167/sample1.csv". Read through the file line by line, incrementing the comment counter when encountering lines starting with "#" (ensuring consecutive comment lines are merged by only incrementing on the first comment in a sequence), and incrementing the record counter for all non-comment lines. After processing the file, construct a CSVFormat using the DEFAULT format as a base and configure it with specific settings: disable missing column names with setAllowMissingColumnNames set to false, set the comment marker to '#', use comma as delimiter, backslash as escape character, define headers as "author", "title", "publishDate", add "headerComment" as a header comment, set null string to "NULL", enable ignoring empty lines and surrounding spaces, use double quote as quote character with QuoteMode set to ALL, set record separator to newline, and disable skipping header records. Parse the same test file using this configured format by creating a CSVParser with the format's parse method, then iterate through all CSVRecord instances, counting both the total records and records that have comments using the hasComment method. Assert that the manually counted comment total equals the parser's comment count using assertEquals, and assert that the manually counted record total equals the parser's record count using assertEquals, noting that the record count includes the header record. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a string variable with the value "$0.map(x -> x * x).reduce((a, x) -> a + x)" which represents a JEXL script that maps each element to its square and reduces by summing. Create a JexlBuilder instance and call its create method to obtain a JexlEngine, then call getUberspect on the engine to retrieve the JexlUberspect. Instantiate an OptionalArithmetic with the boolean value true to handle optional arithmetic operations. Configure a new JexlEngine by calling uberspect on the builder with a new ReferenceUberspect constructed from the previously obtained uberspect, set the arithmetic to the OptionalArithmetic instance, set safe mode to false, and call create to build the engine. Create a JexlInfo object with the name "testStream", line number 1, and column number 1 for debugging information. Initialize a MapContext using the StreamContext subclass to provide the execution context. Call createScript on the engine with the source string and the parameter name "$0" to compile the script. Execute the script by calling execute with the context and a list containing integers 1, 2, and 3 as the argument for parameter "$0". Assert that the result equals the integer value 14, which validates that the stream operations correctly computed 1² + 2² + 3² = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the comprehensive functionality of numeric range objects, specifically testing the creation, boundary management, containment checking, iteration behavior, and immutability enforcement of both LongRange and IntegerRange classes through various assertions and exception handling mechanisms. Initialize the test by setting the Java Util Logging level to SEVERE for the JexlEngine class to suppress non-error logging, then create a LongRange instance using the create method with parameters 20 and 10, which automatically orders the boundaries to produce a range from 10 to 20. Assert that getMin returns 10L and getMax returns 20L, verify that isEmpty returns false, confirm that contains returns true for boundary values 10L and 20L, false for out-of-range values 30L and 5L, and false for null input. Call the helper method checkIteration to validate that iteration proceeds from 20L to 10L in descending order by obtaining an iterator and verifying the first and last values encountered. Create additional LongRange instances with parameters 10 and 20 for ascending iteration testing, and 10 and 15 for subset testing, then assert that the original range contains all elements of both new ranges using containsAll, verify inequality between ranges using assertNotEquals, and confirm proper subset relationships. Repeat the entire sequence with IntegerRange instances using the same boundary values but with integer types, creating ranges with parameters 20 and 10, 10 and 20, and 10 and 15, then validate all the same properties including boundary access, emptiness, containment, iteration order, and subset relationships. Assert that LongRange and IntegerRange instances with identical boundaries are not equal to each other using assertNotEquals to confirm type-specific equality. Iterate through the descending LongRange starting from 20L and decrementing to verify each value matches the expected sequence, while testing immutability by attempting various modification operations including iterator remove, range add, remove, addAll, removeAll, and retainAll methods within a switch statement based on the current iteration value, expecting each operation to throw UnsupportedOperationException which is caught and ignored. Assert that the counter reaches 9L after complete iteration and verify that calling next on the exhausted iterator throws NoSuchElementException using assertThrows. Perform identical iteration and immutability testing on the IntegerRange with integer values starting from 20 and decrementing, confirming the counter reaches 9 and the exhausted iterator throws NoSuchElementException. Complete the test by calling the superclass tearDown method to perform any inherited cleanup operations. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the Test annotation and assertion methods like assertEquals, assertFalse, assertTrue, assertNotEquals, and assertThrows.

Initialize a string variable containing the JEXL expression parseDouble("PHM1".substring(3)).intValue() which demonstrates parsing a double from a substring and converting it to an integer value. Create an instance of I33Arithmetic with the boolean parameter true to enable strict arithmetic mode. Construct a JexlEngine using JexlBuilder with safe mode disabled by calling safe with false and the arithmetic instance set using the arithmetic method, then call create to build the engine. Use the engine's createScript method to parse the source string into a JexlScript object and assert that the script is not null using assertNotNull. Execute the script by calling the execute method with a null context parameter to evaluate the expression, which should extract the substring "1" from "PHM1", parse it as a double value 1.0, and convert it to the integer 1. Assert that the execution result equals the integer value 1 using assertEquals to verify the expression evaluation produces the expected numeric conversion from string to double to integer. This test validates JEXL's ability to chain method calls for string manipulation, numeric parsing, and type conversion within a single expression, using the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a CSV parser and printer to test the handling of multiple character delimiters in CSV processing. Create a string reader containing CSV data with a multi-character delimiter "[|]" separating values like "FirstName[|]LastName[|]Address" followed by a data row "John[|]Smith[|]123 Main St.". Configure a CSV format using the default format builder with the delimiter set to the multi-character string "[|]". Parse the CSV data using a CSV parser built with the configured format and string reader, then iterate through the records to verify that the first record contains "FirstName", "LastName", and "Address" in positions 0, 1, and 2 respectively, and the second record contains "John", "Smith", and "123 Main St." in the same positions. Next, test the printing functionality by creating an Excel CSV format with the multi-character delimiter "[I]", setting headers to "first name", "last name", and "address", configuring a comment marker '#', and adding a header comment "Change delimiter to [I]". Use a CSV printer with this format to print the values from the last parsed record, then assert that the output string matches the expected format including the comment line, headers, and data row with the multi-character delimiter. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the CSV library's ability to handle multi-character delimiters for both parsing and printing operations. Initialize a string reader with CSV data that uses a multi-character delimiter pattern, then configure a CSV format with the default settings but specify the multi-character delimiter. Create a CSV parser using the configured format and string reader, then iterate through the parsed records to verify that each field is correctly separated and extracted according to the multi-character delimiter. Assert that the first record contains the expected header values and the second record contains the corresponding data values. Next, test the printing functionality by creating an Excel-style CSV format configured with a different multi-character delimiter, header definitions, comment marker, and header comments. Use a CSV printer with this format to output the previously parsed record values, then verify that the generated output string matches the expected format including the comment header and properly delimited data fields. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

description: This test validates that the EchoUDPClient properly handles unconnected state by throwing NullPointerException when attempting to send data without an established connection. Initialize an EchoUDPClient instance within a try-with-resources block to ensure automatic resource cleanup, then verify that calling the send method with a zero-length byte array and the local host address obtained from InetAddress.getLocalHost throws a NullPointerException using assertThrows, which confirms the client correctly rejects send operations when not connected to a server. Subsequently, assert that the overloaded send method taking additional length parameter zero also throws NullPointerException when passed the same zero-length byte array and local host address, validating that both send method variants properly enforce connection requirements before attempting UDP datagram transmission to the echo server at the default port. The EchoUDPClient extends DiscardUDPClient and implements UDP-based echo protocol functionality as described in RFC 862, where the send methods internally delegate to a four-parameter send method using the DEFAULT_PORT field value of 7, and the test ensures these methods fail appropriately when the underlying DatagramSocket is not properly connected. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

Immediately capture the suspended time by calling getTime to retrieve the elapsed milliseconds and getDuration to get the elapsed time as a Duration object. Execute another sleep period using the helper method with the same MIN_DURATION plus one millisecond to simulate additional time passing while the watch remains suspended. The helper method sleepPlus1 uses ThreadUtils.sleep to pause execution for the specified duration plus one millisecond to ensure measurable time differences.
